title: How Far? Velocity-Time Graphs Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A bus speedometer, a bowler's speed gun, a bicycle speed meter. All three tell you how fast, none of them tells you how far. So how can Aarav find out how far he rode to college? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn to read a velocity-time graph.

We ride along with Aarav in a live simulation while his v-t graph draws itself: up means speeding up, flat means steady, down means slowing down. We show step by step why the slope of a v-t graph is the acceleration and why the area under it is the displacement (12 + 24 + 9 = 45 m), what it means when the line goes below the time axis, a worked example with a trapezium, the exam trap about lines sloping down, and an original JEE Main pattern question on distance vs displacement with a full solution. Then a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 How fast, but how far?
0:24 What is a velocity-time graph?
0:41 Live ride: the graph draws itself
1:15 Flat line: x-t vs v-t + pause and think
1:45 Slope = acceleration, step by step
2:18 Area = displacement
2:57 Below the time axis + pause and think
3:33 Worked example: the bus
4:06 Exam trap: does sloping down mean backward?
4:31 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:07 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Acceleration-Time Graphs. In a bus you feel the braking, but never the speed. Why?
